subject.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `rawBody` as provenance-gated, command-normalized clean direct-user text even though its name can be read as literal inbound transport text?
rationale: This is an additive external plugin API contract. Tests can prove propagation, but they cannot choose whether the public name and semantics are the product contract maintainers want plugins to depend on.

options.title: Accept the clean-text contract
options.body: Keep `rawBody`, explicitly define it as provenance-gated clean direct-user text, and treat literal transport-body access as out of scope.

options.title: Rename before publishing
options.body: Choose a name such as `cleanUserText` that makes the normalized semantics unambiguous before external plugins begin relying on it.

options.title: Defer the API
options.body: Pause this feature until the broader trusted inbound-body contract has a maintainer-approved plugin-facing design.

recommendation.title: Accept the clean-text contract
recommendation.body: Keep `rawBody`, explicitly define it as provenance-gated clean direct-user text, and treat literal transport-body access as out of scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They can clarify the intended API semantics and implement the chosen narrow adjustment, while final acceptance remains a maintainer product decision.
